data.name: Ayishah
data.gender_notes: Ayishah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ayishah (رضي الله عنها) is the name of the beloved wife of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and one of the most revered women in Islam. She was known for her beauty, grace, wisdom, and devotion to her husband and the faith. The name Ayishah carries the meaning “Mother of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ayishah usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of prophet muhammad (pbuh) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of dedication and loyalty to one's spouse and faith.
data.etymology: Ayishah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mother of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayishah total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_urdu.name: ایشہ
in_urdu.meaning: نیکوکار خاتون اور نبی محمد کی زوجہ

data.cultural_impact: Ayishah was a powerful role model for Muslim women who have become a symbol of love, dignity, and nobility. As a respected figure in Islamic history, Ayishah's name continues to resonate deeply in the hearts of Muslims all around the world. Her story of a loyal and devoted wife to a prophet inspires many, and her reputation for wisdom and intelligence is a reminder of the potential of women in society. Ayishah is celebrated in poetry, art, and literature, and her influence extends beyond Islamic cultures, touching the hearts of people of all backgrounds.
data.spiritual_significance: Ayishah is regarded as a pious and virtuous woman, whose love and devotion to her Prophet became the epitome of the sacred bond between a husband and a wife in Islam. Her life was an embodiment of Islam, and her actions and teachings set an example for generations to come. Her faith, inner strength, and resilience in the face of adversity serve as a reminder of the spiritual depth that every Muslim strives to achieve. Ayishah was a witness to many significant events in Islamic history, including the Hijrah (Migration of the Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Medina), and her presence and actions throughout history continue to be a source of inspiration and guidance for Muslims. May Allah (swt) shower His endless blessings upon our beloved Prophet Muhammad, his noble family, and companions. Aameen.
